title: Canonical truncation comparisons for t-exact triangulated functors
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category] with bounded t-structures [def-weil-t-structure]. Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be an exact functor, with its shift comparison, and suppose that for every $n\in\mathbf Z$ it sends $\mathcal C^{\le n}$ into $\mathcal D^{\le n}$ and $\mathcal C^{\ge n}$ into $\mathcal D^{\ge n}$. Write $\iota^m:\tau^{\le m}\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}$ and $\pi^m:\operatorname{id}\Rightarrow\tau^{\ge m}$ for the canonical maps. There are unique natural isomorphisms
$$
 \alpha^-_{F,m}:F\tau_{\mathcal C}^{\le m}\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau_{\mathcal D}^{\le m}F,
 \qquad
 \alpha^+_{F,m}:F\tau_{\mathcal C}^{\ge m}\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau_{\mathcal D}^{\ge m}F
$$
characterized at each $K$ by
$$
 \iota^m_{FK}\circ\alpha^-_{F,m,K}=F(\iota^m_K),\qquad
 \alpha^+_{F,m,K}\circ F(\pi^m_K)=\pi^m_{FK}.
$$
For any other such functor $G$ and any natural transformation $\eta:F\Rightarrow G$, the comparisons satisfy, for either sign and its corresponding truncation $\tau$,
$$
 \alpha_{G,m,K}\circ\eta_{\tau K}=\tau(\eta_K)\circ\alpha_{F,m,K}.
$$
The comparison for the identity functor is the identity. If $H:\mathcal D\to\mathcal B$ is another exact functor preserving the two halves of bounded t-structures, the comparison for $HF$ is the composite $H(\alpha_F)$ followed by $\alpha_H$ at $FK$.

proof.text: Use Mathlib TStructure.to_truncLT_obj_ext and from_truncGE_obj_ext, the injective forms of the truncation adjunctions of [def-weil-t-structure]. For a general isomorphism e : Y ≅ truncGE n X and u : X → Y satisfying u ≫ e.hom = π_X, derive π_X ≫ e.inv = u. Cancel the isomorphism e.inv and apply from_truncGE_obj_ext. This is the proved private helper cancel_truncGE_unit, giving cancellation of u into any object in the lower aisle.

Iso.ext and natural-transformation extensionality give uniqueness of the natural isomorphism. Exactness is the one in [def-weil-triangulated-category].

proof.text: For η : F → G, the source F(truncLT (m+1) K) has the required upper bound by IsTExact.isLE_obj. Apply to_truncLT_obj_ext to the two upper morphisms. Use G's counit equation, naturality of the truncation counit, F's counit equation, and naturality of η on the source counit to identify their composites.

proof.text: For the lower natural-transformation square, apply step 1's cancellation helper with F's lower comparison and unit image. Naturality of η on the source unit, G's unit equation, F's unit equation, and naturality of the target unit give equality after this precomposition. The target truncGE m (G K) lies in the lower aisle.

proof.text: For identity comparisons βLE and βGE, apply to_truncLT_obj_ext and from_truncGE_obj_ext directly. Their assumed characterizing equations agree with those of the identity morphisms by id_comp and comp_id.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i): elementary identity calculation and uniqueness

proof.text: For the composite, the source H(F(truncLT (m+1) K)) lies in the upper aisle by applying t-exactness of F then H. Apply to_truncLT_obj_ext, use the assumed equation for βLE, then H's counit equation and preservation of composition by H, and finally F's counit equation. For the lower sign apply the step 1 helper with βGE itself and H(F(π_K)); its characterizing equation is an assumption. Map F's unit equation through H and apply H's unit equation. This proves the lower composite equality without constructing any new composite t-exactness instance.
